notes_for_us: The prompt names ten worlds and the handoff can carry the fact that there are ten but not what they are. Small Town, Beach Resort, Space Colony and Candy Kingdom are ten different themes and the theme field holds exactly one string, so nine of them survive only as prose in an option text.

A six-step pizza line is a sequence - dough before sauce before cheese before oven - and trigger-task is a single unordered pick. There is no way to say that the stations run in an order, which is the one spatial fact about a cooking loop that matters.

The whole ten-world structure hangs off teleporter-link, an option whose route varies, and that single judgement call is what puts the build on P4. A structural decision this large arriving through an option rather than the shape feels like the wrong carrier.

The shape choice was between world-open and a per-player plot and the prompt genuinely does not say. Players start with a tiny pizza stand reads as a personal plot; a shared persistent world reads as the simulator convention. The genre notes warn about exactly this and still do not settle it.
